findings.title: [P2] Repeated official verification still rejects its legitimately completed attempt
findings.candidate_rule_id: D-03/D-05/D-07: provider-specific attempt provenance and idempotent administrative verification
findings.rationale:
Source-confirmed counterexample, not a runtime reproduction by this reviewer: perform the normal official NOVO -> authorize -> confirm -> subscribe plus authenticated receipt flow already exercised in number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:37-80. NumberRegistrationService.create creates the official attempt without pairingEpoch (number-registration.service.ts:122-128); the nullable field has no default (schema.prisma:210 and migrations/20261015120000_number_onboarding_foundation/migration.sql:53). The channel epoch defaults to integer 0 (schema.prisma:143; that migration:32). Official credential promotion changes generation/state/stage but never assigns an attempt epoch (number-registration.service.ts:357-363), and completed receipt promotion only changes state/stage/version (message-acceptance.service.ts:141-145 or number-registration.service.ts:430-434). Thus a valid current OFICIAL attempt can be CONNECTED/RECEIPT_VERIFIED, with attempt.pairingEpoch=null, channel.pairingEpoch=0, verified owner, SUBSCRIBED channel, active scoped credential and durable receipt. ChannelsService.verificar reaches its receipt/subscription branch (channels.service.ts:281-292,317-337) and passes 0 to the new helper at line 336. Both helper predicates require pairingEpoch=0 (receipt-attempt-convergence.ts:14,22); null matches neither, so ATTEMPT_STALE at channels.service.ts:337 rolls back the otherwise valid verification. This fails even with the correct tenant, channel, attempt ID, generation and credential; it is a correctness/availability failure, not a demonstrated privilege escalation.

Why now: the changed shared convergence locus and dispatch explicitly cover official as well as unofficial repeated verification. The old inline predicate also contained this null-versus-0 defect; this is an incomplete same-current-contract correction at the changed locus, not a claim that cp36 introduced the original defect or a reopening of unrelated accepted architecture. The two cp36 tests use NAO_OFICIAL (number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:637-690); 501 green tests therefore do not refute this official counterexample. The official baseline positive ends after CONNECTED and does not repeat channel verify. D-03/D-05/D-07 and the current integrations-and-channels recovery paragraph are not fully satisfied by the delivered common helper.
findings.suggested_action:
Recommend A: represent the existing provider-specific epoch contract explicitly in the helper/caller. Official attempt provenance uses the persisted null epoch; Evolution uses the exact numeric current epoch. A nullable expected-epoch argument selected by the already trusted channel type is one small faithful implementation; keep exact attempt ID, generation, CONNECTED/RECEIPT_VERIFIED stage, owner/current-channel fences and transactions. Do not use a broad null-or-any-epoch fallback for Evolution, omit generation/epoch predicates globally, or rewrite operational data. Add a real BFF/PostgreSQL fail-first regression that follows the normal official creation/credential/subscription/authenticated-receipt lifecycle, proves the actual persisted null epoch, then verifies twice with HTTP 200 and unchanged completed attempt version/identity/receipt/currentAttemptId/credential; retain the existing Evolution stale/cancelled/generation/epoch negatives. Refresh frozen hashes and appropriate canonical validation/review after the serial authorized correction. Effort small; risk low if provider applicability is explicit; blast radius the shared helper, administrative caller and flow test; maintenance low; performance still at most one extra PK-scoped lookup; elegance/structural soundness improve by removing a false cross-provider assumption.

B: normalize official attempt epochs to the channel epoch throughout creation/promotion and define handling for existing null rows. Effort/risk/blast radius larger, additional source/data-contract consideration and validation; maintenance higher than A; no intrinsic performance gain; potentially coherent but unnecessary for this bounded correction. C: leave this behavior unchanged. Zero implementation effort and query impact, but legitimate official repeated verification remains broken; maintenance and structural correctness worsen through an undocumented provider exception. C is not recommended and does not satisfy the dispatched contract. Root owns scope admission, implementation authority and final adjudication.

overall_assessment:
One material P2 adherence/correctness finding: NUM-ADH-CP36-01. Return the shared administrative-verification correction for a bounded provider-applicability fix before accepting this delta across both modalities. The Evolution completed-attempt recovery path is coherent on the reviewed source; no new exploitable tenant/authentication regression, secret exposure, unsafe network operation inside a transaction, or broad architecture shortcut was established. This is advisory source review, not overall delivery/recovery/production acceptance.

Scope and evidence: read the dedicated dispatch, its final adherence/security addendum and GO routing artifact at foundation_documentation/artifacts/tmp/number-onboarding-execution/routing-cp36-adherence-security.json. Reviewed the new helper directly and the three named public tracked diffs against f134bd11449a553e6f57e66cdc8fc71032151060, plus only necessary public caller/identity/credential/attempt/receipt/schema/module fences and supplied evidence. Independently recomputed all four source SHA-256 values; each matches cp36-review-source-freeze.json, including helper ab837f4c0b8bca372b598a0e6226acd68db63b1458319c56f5756a292e7dc144. Reviewed root-cp36-validation-receipt.json, cp36-api-recovery-summary.md, final-all terminal/totals, browser attestation and genuine pre-worker freshness manifest. They substantiate the supplied 138 API unit + 288 PostgreSQL + 28 Web unit + 47 browser = 501 local tests and 22 migrations on these bytes; the new helper is present in the pre-worker manifest. No suite, build, provider/runtime call, private dotenv/payload/log access or Git mutation was performed by this reviewer. Only the named result artifact is written. Assurance / Security-Adversarial profile with NestJS, Prisma, PostgreSQL and Docker scope; Genesis is inapplicable to this existing approved contract.

Decision adherence, individually:
D-01 — Adherent in this delta. It adds no BU/tenant creation or ownership transfer. Verify retains same-BU lookup, canonical-phone comparison and locked CAS claim (channels.service.ts:261-275,317-330); webhook derives BU/channel from the durable provider identity.
D-02 — Preserve / unchanged. No SDK, OAuth candidate, capability or client-selection behavior changes; official verification still reads the authorized provider resource using its scoped credential (channels.service.ts:281-292).
D-03 — Exception at repeated official verification: a legitimately completed current attempt fails the common epoch predicate, as NUM-ADH-CP36-01 details. Otherwise the new helper preserves pending promotion and single version increment and adds only exact completed-state acceptance; no nonce/code reuse, new session mechanism or external HTTP within its transaction.
D-04 — Preserve / unchanged. The correction neither reads nor returns secrets. Official verify still uses ChannelCredentialResolver with active generation/version AAD; no global-token fallback or candidate promotion is added.
D-05 — Exception limited to official repeated verification, not a newly introduced registration workflow. The helper must honor the existing null official epoch so valid completed official recovery is idempotent. Register/subscribe sequencing, partial outcomes and callback ownership remain unchanged.
D-06 — Locally adherent for the numeric Evolution epoch correction. The helper accepts only the same attempt/generation/epoch and exact CONNECTED/RECEIPT_VERIFIED pair after existing current-owner/identity/receipt readiness guards. Pending promotion is unchanged. It does not pair, renew, create an instance or trust wuid. Cancelled/wrong-generation/wrong-epoch outcomes remain fail-closed. This source judgment does not close the TODO temporary D-06 runtime Exception: the operator still runs the old API and recovery requires the corrected runtime plus a new human IN/OUT exchange.
D-07 — Mixed: same-generation/epoch observation convergence is preserved for Evolution, while the official applicability mismatch remains a functional exception. Incoming connection observations cannot transfer an external owner or bypass identity/receipt proof. Persisted CONNECTED/receipt is a last observation, not continuous health or proof of a new exchange; same-epoch callback reordering is not newly solved or claimed.
D-08 — Preserve / unchanged. The helper does not create messages/conversations, publish realtime, run Typebot or select credentials. Existing shared receipt/message acceptance, per-resource external-ID unique constraints, ownership checks and transaction rollback remain the owners of those effects. No new publication/automation guarantee is asserted.
D-09 — Adherent within local-source scope. The supplied validation uses the owned disposable local namespace and fresh served bundle. No Railway, external official proof, provider mutation or operational recovery proof follows from this review.
D-10 — Adherent within this review. The four sources remained frozen and hash-matched; no code/canon/Git changes, worktrees, auxiliary checkouts or delegation were performed. The next writer must remain serialized after this reviewer stops.

Module consistency: integrations-and-channels owns this exact idempotent current-attempt recovery contract; its newly explicit paragraph preserves the approved intent and correctly distinguishes last observation from health. The Evolution implementation fits that paragraph, but the official null-epoch counterexample is an unresolved inconsistency at the common caller. identity-and-tenancy ADMIN/session/anti-CSRF and owner boundaries, inbox-and-conversations message/dedupe/publication invariants, and audit-and-history scoped/redacted diagnostic and durable history contracts are preserved by the delta. Prior cp21/cp25/cp27 judgments remain historical for unchanged loci; none was automatically promoted into proof of this new helper.

Security/adversarial assessment: the enclosing TODO remains high risk because the entry points are administrative BFF and authenticated external webhook; attack simulation remains required by the existing TODO. This bounded review performed static abuse-case analysis and read supplied local evidence, without executing attacks. BFF verify still requires ADMIN in the BU, revalidates session/grant after provider reads, uses a bounded operation lease and checks currentAttemptId/generation/epoch at commit (channels.controller.ts:84-113; channels.service.ts:257-344). Webhook authentication remains timing-safe private-header verification before identity lookup, and connection processing locks the durable same-BU identity, BU and channel, re-reads the current generation/epoch and obtains currentAttemptId from that locked row (evolution.controller.ts:25-40,69-75,113-133). Neither caller accepts an attempt ID, BU owner or epoch supplied by an untrusted callback. Server-owned attempt creation/assignment binds the attempt to that BU/channel; creation CAS and RENEW/delete fences were inspected. Exact-attempt provenance is sufficient in these two callers for tenant safety; duplicating tenant fields inside the small helper is not needed to establish a new security finding. The newly admitted completed branch requires exact state and receipt stage, performs no version write, and returns false for CANCELLED/ERROR, wrong generation/epoch or a completed incompatible stage. A false result throws inside the same channel transaction, rolling back the preceding readiness write. Cancellation and provider-identity races in unchanged paths were not reclassified without evidence of a delta-created exploit. Numeric epoch checks must remain strict for Evolution when fixing the official null case. No injection, SSRF, unauthenticated read/write or secret-bearing error path is introduced. Threat-intel refresh was not needed for this source-local state-machine correction: no dependency or cryptographic change is claimed, and known dependency debt is retained rather than newly measured.

Code quality, elegance, structure and concurrency: a single Channels-domain operation with Prisma.TransactionClient removes duplicated promotion semantics from the two callers. Both callers await it inside their existing identity -> BU -> channel transaction/lock order; no new lock order, network call, loop, worker, schema or dependency is introduced. Conditional pending promotion plus a narrow read of an already completed row is clearer than forcing a second promotion or version bump. No performance/elegance regression or workaround-based structural shortcut was established. Structural soundness is mixed solely because the new shared helper assumes a numeric attempt epoch for a caller that legitimately persists null. A small provider-aware contract removes that defect; redesign of the approved feature is not warranted.

Performance position: acceptable as a bounded static assessment. Pending promotion still uses the existing id-scoped update; only a miss performs one additional findFirst with the unique primary-key id, generation, epoch, state and stage, selecting id alone (receipt-attempt-convergence.ts:10-24; schema.prisma:192). Completed replay therefore adds one database round trip while locks are held. There is no collection scan/fan-out contract, new query index need, network inside transaction, cache or new allocation proportional to tenant size. No latency/SLO/load claim or new-helper benchmark is made, and old PCV resolver/EPS samples are not attributed to this lookup.

Tests and evidence boundary: the two new tests align with the real Evolution recovery contract rather than rewriting the expected failure into success. The positive proves a real BFF/pair -> authenticated first IN -> persisted completed attempt and receipt, then repeated verify and connecting/open/duplicate-open, with version/receipt/identity/message assertions. The negative mutates only disposable attempt state/generation/epoch and verifies ATTEMPT_STALE and channel rollback. These are proportionate API/PostgreSQL tests, not new endpoints or production test flags; targeted inspection found no new focused/skip or silent-fallback bypass. helpers.ts:149-162 retains AppModule, real body parsers and Prisma while replacing only existing external provider tokens; this is local contract evidence, not real Meta/Evolution compatibility. The available RED excerpt and pre-edit hashes show the positive failed before production edits at both verify/open loci; the complete RED stdout was not captured and is not recoverable, and the later negative has no claimed RED. Do not fabricate stronger provenance. The missing official repeat is a coverage limit tied to the concrete code finding, not a blanket rejection of the independent TQA. I did not read the TQA live output or result; root separately reported its terminal status, and it does not waive this architecture finding. Claimed platform evidence is local Windows/WSL/Docker, Node22/OpenSSL3 and PostgreSQL16; no Railway/mobile/device/official-OAuth matrix completion is inferred.

P1/P2 and Rule-Spirit: no new P1 security/data-loss finding established; one P2 functional blocker remains at the changed shared locus. The helper is a faithful convergence abstraction, with no swallow-error fallback, fake webhook on the operator, manual DB repair, blind OAuth retry, global credential, new generic job architecture or version bump merely to satisfy a test. Genuine local green/freshness evidence and the RED capture limitation are distinguished. Fix the official applicability rather than weaken epoch matching or expand acceptance to arbitrary completed states.

Debt and operational fit: the older mixed/test-after debt TQA-CP21-02 remains recorded; cp36 has genuine pre-fix positive evidence with its explicit raw-log limitation, and the new official regression should capture authentic RED. Existing dependency audit debt (8 affected: 1 critical, 6 high, 1 moderate; authenticated Multer DoS) remains restricted to the private OWNER/synthetic cohort under BLG-leadshug-runtime-dependency-security and due before untrusted authenticated users; it is not fixed or freshly audited here. The post-commit/pre-publication crash gap, no outbox and no automatic replay remain approved limitations. VAL-05 official OAuth/IN/OUT/recovery remains mandatory and unwaived. First human unofficial IN/OUT is accepted historical evidence; corrected-runtime recovery and a fresh human exchange remain pending. Overall TODO stays Pending; neither NUM-RECOVERY-CP36-01 nor its temporary exception is closed by this report.
